title: Design: New Work Order for a COD customer shows no warning
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create customer A for this test, on COD with a $0.00 credit limit and an unpaid balance.
  • Create an asset for customer A for this test, asset A.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Open the attached design picture ct-p8-02-cod-customer-0-limit-owes-1-200-no-warning.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
  • Start on the customer page of customer A.
custom_steps:
1. Click "New Work Order".
  2. Choose asset A in Asset.
  3. Click "Save".
  4. Resize the browser window to 1536 px wide (for example, maximise it on a 1536 x 864 screen at 100% zoom).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The "New Work Order" window opens with Customer A (as in ct-p8-02-cod-customer-0-limit-owes-1-200-no-warning.png).

Step 2:

  • Asset reads asset A.

Step 3:

  • The work order opens.
  • No "Confirmation" window appears.

Step 4:

  • At 1536 px nothing overlaps, nothing is cut off and nothing needs a sideways scroll.
  • The layout described above is unchanged, only wider.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11678 (Story 9, Over Credit warning)

  • S9-N1: “The warning and the badge never show when the customer's credit limit is $0 or blank.”
  • S9-N2: “The warning and the badge never show for a customer on COD, Due on Receipt or Credit Hold, whatever their limit or balance. A customer with a blank term counts as COD.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "8 Over Credit warning" ("COD customer, $0 limit, owes $1,200: no warning"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes, except where this held design case follows the design.

The design's own words:
